We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We have guidance: three steps: (1) amide formation from carboxylic acid + amine (forward). So retrosynthesis: break amide to give carboxylic acid and amine.

(2) Doebner modification: aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid (the new alkene). So retrosynthesis: break the C=C and carboxylic acid to give aromatic aldehyde and malonic acid.

(3) Sulfonamide formation: amine + sulfonyl chloride -> sulfonamide. So retrosynthesis: break sulfonamide to give amine and sulfonyl chloride.

Thus overall target: aromatic sulfonamide attached to phenyl ring with para methyl (tolyl) and sulfonyl attached to second phenyl ring bearing α,β-unsaturated carboxamide side chain.

We need to propose precursors for each step.

Step 1 (retro amide): target contains C(=O)N attached to an aniline (c3ccccc3N). The amide is attached to the unsaturated chain: /C=C/C(=O)N-Ph-NH2? Actually SMILES: .../C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N . So the amide carbonyl attached to N which is attached to an aniline (aniline with NH2). So retro: break amide to give carboxylic acid (the α,β-unsaturated acid) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). So precursor 1: α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/CO)cc2)cc1? Wait the unsaturated acid would be: /C=C/COOH attached to phenyl sulfonyl? Actually the unsaturated acid is attached to the sulfonyl phenyl via the double bond: the chain is phenyl-sulfonyl-phenyl-CH=CH-COOH? Let's parse: target: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

So we have tolyl (methyl phenyl) attached to sulfonamide N (NSO2). The sulfonyl attached to second phenyl ring (c2ccc(... )cc2). That phenyl has substituent /C=C/C(=O)N-Ph-NH2 at para position? The SMILES shows /C=C/C(=O)N... attached to phenyl as side chain.

Thus retro step 1: break amide: product -> unsaturated carboxylic acid attached to phenyl (the side chain) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). So unsaturated acid: phenyl-CH=CH-COOH (para to sulfonyl). So precursor A: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/CO)cc2)cc1? Wait the unsaturated acid would be phenyl-CH=CH-COOH, not CO? Actually the side chain is /C=C/C(=O)N... So after breaking amide, we get /C=C/COOH attached to phenyl. So the SMILES for that fragment: c2ccc(/C=C/CO)cc2 attached to sulfonyl. So full precursor after step1: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/CO)cc2)cc1 . That's a phenyl-sulfonamide with unsaturated acid.

Step 2 (retro Doebner): break unsaturated acid to give aromatic aldehyde and malonic acid. The unsaturated acid is phenyl-CH=CH-COOH. Doebner modification forward: aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid. So retro: phenyl-CH=CH-COOH -> phenyl-CHO (benzaldehyde) + malonic acid (HOOC-CH2-COOH). So precursor B: benzaldehyde (maybe p-substituted? The phenyl is attached to sulfonyl at para? Actually the phenyl bearing the side chain is attached to sulfonyl at position 1, side chain at para? In SMILES: c2ccc(/C=C/CO)cc2 . The side chain is at position 1? The phenyl is attached to sulfonyl at position 1, side chain at position 4 (para). So the aldehyde precursor would be the same phenyl with aldehyde at para: c2ccc(C=O)cc2 (para-aldehyde). So we need p-formyl phenyl sulfonyl? Actually the sulfonyl attaches to phenyl at position 1, aldehyde at para. So precursor: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(C=O)cc2)cc1 . That's the sulfonamide with aldehyde.

Step 3 (retro sulfonamide formation): break sulfonamide to give amine (toluidine) and sulfonyl chloride (p-chlorosulfonyl phenyl? Actually sulfonyl chloride attached to phenyl with aldehyde). The sulfonamide is NS(=O)(=O) attached to tolyl (methyl phenyl) on nitrogen side, and attached to phenyl ring (the sulfonyl phenyl). So retro: break N-S bond to give tolyl amine (p-toluidine) and sulfonyl chloride (p-formyl phenyl sulfonyl chloride). So precursor C: p-toluidine (4-methylaniline) SMILES: Cc1ccc(N)cc1 . And sulfonyl chloride: p-formyl phenyl sulfonyl chloride: c1ccc(S(=O)(=O)Cl)cc1C=O? Actually aldehyde at para to sulfonyl chloride. So SMILES: O=CC1=CC=C(S(=O)(=O)Cl)C=C1? Wait need correct: aromatic ring with aldehyde and sulfonyl chloride para to each other. So SMILES: O=CC1=CC=C(S(=O)(=O)Cl)C=C1 . That's 4-formylbenzenesulfonyl chloride.

Thus the three-step retrosynthesis:

Target -> (1) amide disconnection -> precursor1 (unsaturated acid) + aniline.

Precursor1 -> (2) Doebner disconnection -> aldehyde phenyl + malonic acid.

Precursor2 (aldehyde phenyl attached to sulfonyl) -> (3) sulfonamide disconnection -> p-toluidine + p-formylbenzenesulfonyl chloride.

Now we need to construct JSON route with 3 reaction nodes.

We need template IDs for each step. We can search for templates matching these transformations.

Step 3: sulfonamide formation (amine + sulfonyl chloride). Search for functional_groups_formed: ["sulfonamides"], broken: maybe ["alkyl halide"]? Already we have template 1313644 from earlier search that is sulfonamide formation from aryl halide? It shows Cl-[S...]-[c] + amine -> sulfonamide. That seems appropriate: reactants: aryl chloride sulfonyl chloride? Actually the template shows Cl-[S...]-[c] + amine -> sulfonamide attached to aryl. So we can use template_id 1313644.

Step 2: Doebner modification (aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid). Need template that forms C-C double bond and carboxylic acid from aldehyde and malonic acid. Search for functional_groups_formed: ["C-C double bonds"], broken: maybe ["carboxylic acid"]? Not correct. Let's search for templates with functional_groups_formed: ["C-C double bonds"] and functional_groups_broken: ["carboxylic esters"]? Not sure. Could search for "aldehydes" broken? Actually forward reaction: aldehyde + malonic acid -> unsaturated acid, so broken: "carboxylic acid"? malonic acid loses CO2 (decarboxylation) so a carboxylic acid is broken (one CO2). So broken: "carboxylic acid". Formed: "C-C double bonds". So we need template that matches that. Let's search.
